plan.topic: Semaglutide 7.2 mg (Wegovy HD) vs tirzepatide (Zepbound): has there been a head-to-head trial? The SURMOUNT-5 dose gap explained
plan.angle: Answer by 10 s: 'No. Semaglutide 7.2 mg hasn't been tested against tirzepatide in a randomized trial. The only head-to-head, SURMOUNT-5, used semaglutide at up to 2.4 mg.' SURMOUNT-5 (adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks, maximum tolerated doses): tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg 20.2% vs semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg 13.7%. STEP UP (adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks): semaglutide 7.2 mg 18.7% vs semaglutide 2.4 mg 15.6% (treatment-policy). Novo reported 20.7% for 7.2 mg (trial-product). Label it 'Separate trials, not head-to-head.' FDA approved 7.2 mg in Mar 2026 for adults who've tolerated 2.4 mg and need more weight loss. Optional neutral lawsuit line: 'Novo Nordisk is suing Lilly over these ad comparisons; Lilly disputes it; no ruling yet.' One GI line, 'don't switch or stop on your own', and the prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Semaglutide 7.2 mg (Wegovy HD) vs Tirzepatide (Zepbound): Ever Tested Head to Head? #shorts
plan.why: Our proven named head-to-head lane (SURMOUNT-5 at 157 and growing) gets a fresh, rising hook from the lawsuit headlines. It's a myth-correcting piece that names both drugs and both doses. | fact-check: A useful, accurate correction that fits the head-to-head lane. Checked: the FDA approved Wegovy HD (semaglutide 7.2 mg) in Mar 2026 (HCPLive 19 Mar 2026) for adults with obesity or overweight who have tolerated 2.4 mg for at least 4 weeks and need more weight loss. STEP UP: 1,407 adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks. Weight loss was 18.7% on 7.2 mg vs 15.6% on 2.4 mg (treatment-policy), and Novo reported 20.7% for the trial-product estimand. Novo sued Lilly in Jul 2026 (D.N.J., Lanham Act), alleging that ads compared Zepbound's top doses with lower Wegovy doses. Lilly says it stands behind the SURMOUNT-5-based ads and there's no verdict yet (Reuters via CTV and others). Fixes: (a) SURMOUNT-5's semaglutide arm was the maximum tolerated dose of 1.7 or 2.4 mg, and tirzepatide was 10 or 15 mg. Saying only '2.4 mg' overstates it, so use 'semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg (maximum tolerated)'; (b) STEP UP compared 7.2 mg with 2.4 mg and placebo, not with tirzepatide; (c) present both STEP UP estimands with labels, treatment-policy 18.7% first; (d) give the approval population as 'adults who have tolerated 2.4 mg and need more weight loss'; (e) source the lawsuit to a confirmed primary news report. The Pharmaphorum article wasn't located, so use Reuters/CTV or verify Pharmaphorum before citing it, and include Lilly's response. Keep it under 170 words: drop the lawsuit if it pushes the script over.

package.title: Semaglutide 7.2 mg vs Tirzepatide: Tested Head-to-Head? #shorts
package.description:
No randomized trial has tested semaglutide 7.2 mg head-to-head against tirzepatide (as of Oct 2026); 7.2 mg wasn't in SURMOUNT-5. In SURMOUNT-5 (72 weeks, adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes), at maximum tolerated doses: tirzepatide 10/15 mg 20.2% (n=374) vs semaglutide 1.7/2.4 mg 13.7% (n=377) body-weight loss. Semaglutide 7.2 mg was FDA-approved in March 2026; gastrointestinal effects like nausea were most common.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Don't switch or stop on your own; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

- The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology 2025: STEP UP trial
- FDA Drugs@FDA, NDA 215256
- Healio 2026: FDA approves high-dose Wegovy 7.2 mg

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe, and the hook gets the payoff it promises. Three small fixes are listed below.

**SURMOUNT-5 checks out** (NEJM 2025, Aronne et al.):
- 72 weeks.
- Adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes.
- Maximum tolerated doses: tirzepatide 10/15 mg (n=374) vs semaglutide 1.7/2.4 mg (n=377).
- Weight loss of 20.2% vs 13.7%.
- Gastrointestinal effects were the most common side effects.

**STEP UP checks out** (Wharton et al., Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology 2025):
- 72 weeks, BMI ≥30, no diabetes.
- 1,005 on 7.2 mg vs 201 on 2.4 mg.
- 18.7% vs 15.6% when everyone randomised is counted (treatment-policy figure), and an estimated 20.7% vs 17.5% if everyone stayed on treatment (trial-product estimand).

**The FDA approval checks out.** Wegovy HD 7.2 mg was approved on 19 March 2026. Drugs@FDA lists it as NDA 215256 SUPPL-29, "Efficacy-New Dosing Regimen", and lists the Wegovy HD 7.2 mg/0.75 mL product.

**"No randomized head-to-head" is correct as of October 2026.** Pharmacy Times covered an indirect comparison presented at EASD in September 2026 and says plainly that "no randomized trial has yet compared the 2 drugs at these doses".

**Framing is good.** The script calls them "separate trials", shows both estimands, tags every number with its drug and dose, and dates the status. The prescriber line and the "don't switch or stop" line are both there.

**Fixes:**
- **Scene s7:** the label says adults who have tolerated 2.4 mg for at least 4 weeks; "already doing well on 2.4" says something different.
- **Scene s2:** two of its source tags don't say the line they're attached to.
- **Source s2:** the URL is a DOI redirect, not the publisher's page.

The narration is about 169 words, right at the 170-word limit, so the fix below trims words rather than adding them.

issues.claim: "as a step up for some adults already doing well on 2.4, when their prescriber decides more weight loss is needed"
issues.problem: The FDA wording is for adults who have tolerated 2.4 mg for at least 4 weeks and need more weight loss. "Doing well" is vague and doesn't match the label's "tolerated". Minor scope drift.
issues.fix: Narration: "7.2 milligrams was FDA-approved in March 2026, as a step up for some adults who've tolerated 2.4, when their prescriber decides more weight loss is needed. Gastrointestinal effects, like nausea, were most common in both trials." (This saves 2 words and keeps the Short at 170 words or fewer.) Change list item 2 to: "A step up after tolerating 2.4 mg".

issues.claim: "As of October 2026, no randomized trial has tested semaglutide 7.2 milligrams against tirzepatide" tagged to s1, s2 and s4
issues.problem: The NEJM SURMOUNT-5 paper (s1) and the STEP UP paper (s2) came out in 2025 and can't back up a status as of October 2026. Only Pharmacy Times (s4) states it.
This DOI link redirects to Elsevier's linking hub. The house rule asks for the final canonical URL with no redirect.
issues.fix: Replace it with https://www.thelancet.com/journals/landia/article/PIIS2213-8587(25)00226-8/fulltext. The page is paywalled, but s4 and s5 confirm the STEP UP figures. Keep the title and year as they are.

approved_by: editor-in-chief (low risk): The hold was a false alarm. Every subtitle "mismatch" is the voice saying a word ("versus", "milligrams", "point") where the subtitle shows the symbol or number ("vs", "mg", "20.2%"), which is how house rules want captions written.
